## Post-hoc notes (written after the held-out run; NOT pre-registered, they change no verdict)

1. **The PIT band in the prereg was mis-specified.** "Each decile within 10–12%" cannot be met unless
   the PIT is exactly uniform: deciles always average 10%, so any decile under 10% fails. The verdict
   stays **NO as written**. For information only: across both held-out seasons and all 8 stats, the
   deciles run 0.084–0.107, inside a ±2-point band (8–12%). The 80% intervals over-cover the
   low-count stats (fg3m, stl, blk, tov: 0.94–0.96). Integer quantiles of a discrete distribution are
   inclusive, so they cover more than 80% by construction.
2. **The tuning-season blend gain did not hold.** On 2023-24 the blend beat the close by 0.0005 log loss
   (in-sample, w chosen there). On held-out 2024-25 it is 0.0004 *worse* than the close (interval
   above zero). The model's information is already in FanDuel's −29 min price.
3. **Why the model alone is overconfident at book lines.** Its own distribution is calibrated (PIT).
   But a line is set with information the historical model lacks: injuries, lineups and late
   minutes news. Conditional on where the line sits, outcomes regress toward it. So the page shows the
   blend at book lines, labeled, with the model alone in grey.
4. **What a better version would need.** Any change to the model is a new version. It needs a new
   pre-registration and is judged on data it has not seen: the forward record from 2026-10-26 on.
   2024-25 and 2025-26 are spent for proj-1.0.

## Limits

The historical market (−29 min) knows injuries and lineups the historical model does not; the model has no injury input. Historical minutes are whole numbers; positions are static. 2025-26 has no historical lines. The 2026-27 replay is a point-in-time reconstruction over a few nights, not the prospective test.
